record_id.reason: Licence Number has 20000 distinct values across 23169 rows, so it is not a unique row key. Each row is hashed instead.

fields.reason: The Licensee column is the licence holder's name, which is the registered licensee and therefore legal_name. Individual licensees (e.g. 'EDWARDS NADIA') are mapped as legal_name without inferring entity type. Names truncated in the source (e.g. 'PTY LIMIT') are passed through as received.

No explicit entity-type column exists (Licence Category and Trading Hours are licence classes, not entity types), so the rule is derived from the Licensee suffix. Pty Ltd/Limited gives company, otherwise unknown. Individuals, associations and truncated suffixes will be unknown.
'Trading As' is the name the business trades under, which is the trading name. It is a single name per row with no splitting needed. Blank values (0.8% of rows) are absent.

Joining Street Address with Suburb is kept because address.full should be a complete premises line, and Street Address alone lacks the suburb. The Street Address-only alternative is rejected for that reason. State is not included because no state column exists in the source.
Suburb is the premises locality. Values are upper-cased, though some sample rows are in mixed case.

Premises postcode. The postcode transform restores dropped leading zeros. The value '0' (229 rows in the full dataset) is not a postcode and will be rejected by the transform. It is not guessed or nulled.

unmapped.reason: No ontology field for a licence number. Retained in the raw record for traceability. Not unique, so not used as record_id.
No ontology field for licence class. Would need a classification field that does not exist in this ontology slice.
No ontology field for trading hours or conditions.
No ontology field for patron capacity.
Correspondence address of the licensee, not the premises. The ontology has no postal address field, and mapping it to address.full would conflate two different addresses.
Correspondence address component, not premises. No ontology field.
Correspondence address component, not premises. No ontology field.
Local government area. No ontology field.
Liquor regulatory region. No ontology field.
Geocoordinate. No ontology field in this slice.
Geocoordinate. No ontology field in this slice.

needs_transform.why: Every row is a Victorian premises, so address.state should be VIC, but no constant-value transform exists. The state is left unmapped until one is available.

source_reliability_basis: Liquor Control Victoria is the statutory regulator that issues and records these licences, so identity (licensee and trading name) is high. Premises addresses are reliable at the time of the snapshot but can go stale, so address is a little lower. The classification score is a publisher-level judgement only: licence category is not mapped in this ontology slice, so it is not used by any field. No contact fields are mapped, so contact is a neutral 0.5.

changes.what: address.full reason rewritten to state why the Street Address-only proposal was rejected. The join with Suburb is kept.
changes.why: The two held-out proposals disagreed. Street Address alone is a street line, not a full address, so proposal 2 would mislabel it. Proposal 1 matches the ontology meaning of address.full, so the config is unchanged in substance.

changes.what: source_reliability_basis reworded so the classification score is not described as backed by a mapped field.
changes.why: Licence Category is unmapped in this slice, so no classification claim is emitted from this source. The numeric scores are unchanged.

warning_responses.reason: The rejections are consistent with postcode value '0', which is not a valid Australian postcode. Rejecting it is correct, and the config does not map it to a guessed value.
Proposal 1 (Street Address joined with Suburb) is kept because it is the complete premises line. Proposal 2 (Street Address alone) is rejected because it lacks suburb.
Licence Number repeats (20000 distinct across 23169 rows), so hash_row remains true. No other column combination was shown to be unique.
No constant-value transform exists, so address.state stays in needs_transform rather than being guessed.
